Chapter 10: Lessons in the Light — What the Golden Spruce Still Teaches
Over the years, the story of the golden spruce has become part of everyday life on Haida Gwaii. You’ll hear it shared in classrooms, whispered over kitchen tables, and honored in songs and ceremonies. But more than anything, it lives on in the hearts of people who once knew the tree. Its meaning? Well, that’s shifted and deepened with time—turning into a touchstone, something folks turn to when they want to reflect or grow.
Imagine this: A young parent is walking along the riverbank with their child. They stop and gently point to the very spot where the golden spruce once stood tall. The child listens, eyes wide—there’s wonder there, and a bit of sadness, too. In that quiet moment, the story becomes more than just history. It’s a lesson. Not just about losing something beautiful, but about really paying attention—and caring for what matters most.
For so many people, the golden spruce is a powerful reminder. It shows us that beauty and meaning are fragile. The choices we make, both as individuals and as a community, can echo for years. It’s made it clear—the land isn’t just something to use up. It’s alive. It deserves to be honored and protected.
But you know, the story doesn’t end with loss. There’s hope woven in, too. In the efforts to restore the forest, to heal old wounds, and to build new, stronger relationships, people have found a renewed sense of purpose and connection. The golden spruce itself may be gone, but its legacy? That endures—in every action of those who remember it and choose to care.
